analysis:
Reviewed both primary analyses and all replayed source/metadata. changelog.d/qwen-end-of-prompt-checkpoints.md:3–13 and docs/architecture/inference.md:1387 describe a new dense-Qwen end-of-prompt checkpoint boundary, gated by the complete store's effective-token floor. The documented boundary is on a 256-token grid, at least 64 tokens before prompt end, and requires 1,024 tokens of benefit. libs/mlx-swift-lm:1 advances the native dependency; the factory replay contains metadata only. These changes do not independently establish a weakened security control or concrete regression.
Against T-041/A-001/TB-007, deeper checkpoints can increase cached prefix depth and affect the accepted same-account timing oracle, but supplied evidence does not establish changes to authenticated scope, HMAC naming, encryption, TTL, donation eligibility or purge. No observed change establishes altered serving authorization, attestation, transport encryption or billing. Checkpoint correctness, cancellation and transient-memory bounds also concern T-007, T-010 and A-018.
The local questions remain unresolved: executable factory and native scheduler/capture changes are absent, and replay omits five reviewed units, including the prefix-cache documentation excerpts. Further review should inspect EngineV2Factory+DemandedCheckpoint.swift:61–79 and its assembly wiring, plus the native dependency diff, to verify floor propagation, projection/scheduler agreement, complete recurrent-state capture, media/packing/preemption exclusions, cancellation and memory charging. Preserve existing authenticated cache scope, model/layout bindings, exact-versus-lossy separation and SSD publication/admission guards. Missing implementation evidence is a material coverage limit, not proof of a vulnerability or safety.
